chunks: What al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Harun ibn Kharijah, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: Were it not that I fear causing hardship to my Ummah, I would have delayed the 'atamah prayer until one-third of the night. And you are under a concession until midnight, and that is the deep darkness of the night. So when the darkness has passed, two angels call out: Whoever has slept away from the prescribed prayer after midnight, may his eyes not sleep.

key_terms.غَسَقُ اللَّيْلِ: the deep darkness of the night
key_terms.مَلَكَانِ: two angels who proclaim the warning
key_terms.نِصْفِ اللَّيْلِ: midnight, the upper limit mentioned here

ai.seo_question: Until what time may the 'isha' prayer be delayed according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the timing of the 'isha' prayer and indicates that delaying it up to midnight falls within a permitted concession. It also strongly warns against neglecting the obligatory prayer beyond midnight, emphasizing the seriousness of missing salat through sleep.
